propositions: The decision_flips metric at parity.py:107 counts an errored pair as a flip when the synthetic decision ('dropped') differs from the other side's verdict, because it compares decision fields without guarding against errored records.

A single transient runtime error (e.g., ThrottlingException) fails the parity slot as a model-quality regression because it triggers criterion (b), which requires zero decision-level flips and treats any flip as never acceptable.
The gold_pairs filter at parity.py:105 admits pairs based on the gold label alone, never inspecting the decision field, so no value of decision can exempt an errored pair from being scored as a flip.

An errored record with errored=True and valid=True silently produces a fabricated flip with no corroborating signal in error_rate or validity metrics, making it impossible for readers to distinguish real flips from fabricated ones.

The reported gating failure strings are byte-identical for three scenarios: (A) 3 real flips / 0 errors, (B) 2 real + 1 error, (C) 0 real / 3 errors, preventing readers from locating which pairs errored.
